es: Resolver un caso final de entrada C1: interpretar lo implícito de un mensaje, responder con tacto y defender una postura con matiz.

vocabulary.es: andar con pies de plomo, mantener un equilibrio delicado

teaching.en: When I read the landlord's message twice, I began to interpret the polite wording as a gentle complaint about the state of the garden.
teaching.es: Cuando leí dos veces el mensaje de la casera, empecé a interpretar su cortés redacción como una queja suave sobre el estado del jardín.
teaching.explanationEs: Interpretar es el primer paso: tono, registro y lo que se sugiere sin decirlo.
segments: When I read the landlord's message twice, I began to interpret the
polite wording as a gentle complaint about the state of the garden.
teaching.audioText: When I read the landlord's message twice, I began to interpret the polite wording as a gentle complaint about the state of the garden.

teaching.en: Her email never said that I was late, but it implied that I should have arrived earlier, so I had to read between the lines.
teaching.es: Su correo nunca decía que yo llegaba tarde, pero daba a entender que debí llegar antes, así que tuve que leer entre líneas.
teaching.explanationEs: Imply + that + oración: sugerir sin decirlo; no se dice implied me. Read between the lines: captar lo no dicho.
segments: Her email never said that I was late, but it implied that I
should have arrived earlier, so I had to read between the lines.
teaching.audioText: Her email never said that I was late, but it implied that I should have arrived earlier, so I had to read between the lines.

teaching.en: I have to tread a fine line here: I admit that the landlord's costs have risen, although I take issue with the claim that the rent rise is unavoidable.
teaching.es: Tengo que andar con pies de plomo: admito que los costos del casero han subido, aunque discrepo de la afirmación de que la subida del alquiler sea inevitable.
teaching.explanationEs: Tread a fine line: equilibrio delicado entre firmeza y cortesía; admit reconoce un punto débil, y take issue with discrepa con educación.
segments: I have to tread a fine line here: I admit that the landlord's costs have
risen, although I take issue with the claim that the rent rise is unavoidable.
teaching.audioText: I have to tread a fine line here: I admit that the landlord's costs have risen, although I take issue with the claim that the rent rise is unavoidable.

teaching.en: Thank you for your generous offer; nevertheless, I must decline, because the dates clash with another commitment I cannot move.
teaching.es: Gracias por tu generosa oferta; sin embargo, debo rechazarla, porque las fechas coinciden con otro compromiso que no puedo mover.
teaching.explanationEs: Reconoce primero y rechaza después con decline y nevertheless: tacto y claridad.
segments: Thank you for your generous offer; nevertheless, I must decline,
because the dates clash with another commitment I cannot move.
teaching.audioText: Thank you for your generous offer; nevertheless, I must decline, because the dates clash with another commitment I cannot move.

teaching.en: To hold your ground without sounding rude, acknowledge the other person's concern first and only then state your position clearly.
teaching.es: Para mantenerte firme sin parecer grosero, reconoce primero la preocupación de la otra persona y solo después expón tu postura con claridad.
teaching.explanationEs: Hold your ground: no ceder en lo esencial; el orden (reconocer, luego postura) protege la relación.
segments: To hold your ground without sounding rude, acknowledge the other
person's concern first and only then state your position clearly.
teaching.audioText: To hold your ground without sounding rude, acknowledge the other person's concern first and only then state your position clearly.

teaching.en: Writing with tact means you strike a balance between honesty and courtesy, and a little nuance shows that you have weighed both sides.
teaching.es: Escribir con tacto significa encontrar un equilibrio entre la sinceridad y la cortesía, y un poco de matiz demuestra que has sopesado ambas partes.
teaching.explanationEs: Strike a balance: encontrar el punto medio; nuance es la mezcla de concesión, cautela y firmeza.
segments: Writing with tact means you strike a balance between honesty and courtesy,
and a little nuance shows that you have weighed both sides.

prompt.es: Interpreta el mensaje: ¿qué da a entender el compañero?

choices.text: He sincerely believes that everybody has been too busy, and sees no problem.
He politely implies that somebody forgot to update the calendar.
He is asking colleagues to empty the calendar so that it can be updated.

feedback.es: No acusa a nadie, pero «left blank again» y «I am sure everybody has had a lot on» sugieren con cortesía que alguien olvidó rellenarlo; tomarlo al pie de la letra sería no leer entre líneas.

hint.es: Fíjate en lo que dice sobre el calendario sin pedirlo directamente.

origin.text: Note from a colleague: I see that the shared calendar has been left blank again this week. I am sure that everybody has had a lot on.

prompt.es: Completa: «Nunca dice que está molesta, pero hay que leer entre líneas.»

feedback.es: Read between the lines es captar lo que un mensaje sugiere sin decirlo de forma explícita.

hint.es: La preposición significa «entre» y aparece en la enseñanza.

origin.text: Your manager's email never says that she is unhappy with you, but you have to read ___ the lines.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Gracias por la oferta; sin embargo, debo rechazarla.»

answer.text: Thank you for the offer nevertheless I must decline it

feedback.es: Se agradece primero, y nevertheless introduce el rechazo con decline: cortés pero claro.

hint.es: Empieza agradeciendo y deja nevertheless para el rechazo.

prompt.es: Escucha el mensaje: ¿qué quiere decir en realidad Elena?

choices.text: She is sincerely reassuring him that the bins were not a problem at all.
She is warning him that the council will fine everyone for blocked pavements.
She is politely complaining and hopes it will not happen again.

feedback.es: Elena suaviza la queja («I am sure it was just a mistake») pero deja claro que los contenedores bloquearon la acera: es una queja cortés, no una tranquilización.

origin.audio: Hi, it is Elena from upstairs. I hope you do not mind me mentioning this, but I could not help noticing that the recycling bins were still on the pavement on Friday morning. I am sure it was just a mistake, and I know how busy this month has been for everybody. It is only that the pavement was blocked for a while. Anyway, thanks so much, and I hope you have a lovely weekend.

prompt.es: Elige la respuesta que agradece, reconoce sus costos y defiende tu postura.

choices.text: Thank you for explaining. I understand your costs; nevertheless, could we discuss a smaller rise?
Thank you for explaining. I understand your costs, so I accept the rise without any question.
Thank you for explaining, but the rise is unfair, and I expect you to cancel it.

feedback.es: Agradece, reconoce el problema del casero y propone hablar: es cortés y defiende su postura; una respuesta cede sin más y la otra exige sin matiz.

origin.text: Your landlord writes: From next month the rent will rise, as our costs have gone up. I trust that this will not be a problem.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con su función en la respuesta final.

pairs: Thank you for letting me know.
I am afraid I must decline.
On balance, I think the plan is fair.
Could we agree to meet on Friday?

feedback.es: Thank you reconoce, I am afraid I must decline rechaza con suavidad, on balance matiza la postura y Could we agree…? propone un acuerdo.

pairs: Thank you for letting me know.
I am afraid I must decline.
On balance, I think the plan is fair.
Could we agree to meet on Friday?

choices.text: That he leaves the report as it is, because it was already detailed.
That he revises the cost section before the board meets on Thursday.
That he postpones sending the report until after the board meeting.

feedback.es: «I did wonder whether the section on costs might benefit from more explanation» es una petición cortés: quiere que lo revise antes del jueves.

origin.text: Dear Tom, thank you for your report, which was, as always, detailed. I did wonder whether the section on costs might benefit from a little more explanation, and perhaps a second pair of eyes before it goes to the board on Thursday. No rush, of course. Kind regards, Helen.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué postura defiende la hablante.

choices.text: She rejects the plan completely and proposes a smaller scheme.
She is unsure about the plan and asks for another proposal.
She defends the plan while admitting that it has some flaws.

feedback.es: Admite que el plan no es perfecto, pero mantiene con firmeza que es la opción más justa: postura defendida con matiz.

origin.audio: I admit that the plan is not perfect, and I can see why some residents are anxious. Even so, I firmly believe that it is the fairest option we have. A smaller scheme would hardly make a difference, whereas doing nothing would cost us far more in the long run.

prompt.es: Completa: «No quiero ser grosero, pero debo discrepar de las cifras de tu informe.»

feedback.es: Take issue with es la colocación para discrepar de algo con educación pero con claridad.

origin.text: I do not want to sound rude, but I must ___ issue with the figures in your report.

prompt.es: Responde al mensaje con tacto y defiende tu postura con matiz.

answer.text: Hi Sam, thank you for your message. I think you are saying that the cleaning is not shared fairly, and I understand why you feel that way. It is true that I have been out a lot this month, and I admit that some weeks you have done more than your part. However, I firmly believe that the problem is partly my work schedule, because I finish late on most days and I am often too tired to clean. To some extent, that may explain why the flat looks worse than before. I am afraid I cannot clean every day, but I would like to find a fair solution. I also want to say that I appreciate how much you have done, and I do not want this to become a bigger problem between us. Could we agree to make a weekly calendar? I could take the kitchen on Saturdays, and you could choose another task. What do you think? Let us review the plan in two weeks. Thanks again for being honest with me.
accepted: Hi Sam, thank you for your message. I think you are saying that the cleaning is not shared fairly, and I understand why you feel that way. It is true that I have been out a lot this month, and I admit that some weeks you have done more than your part. However, I firmly believe that the problem is partly my work schedule, because I finish late on most days and I am often too tired to clean. To some extent, that may explain why the flat looks worse than before. I am afraid I cannot clean every day, but I would like to find a fair solution. I also want to say that I appreciate how much you have done, and I do not want this to become a bigger problem between us. Could we agree to make a weekly calendar? I could take the kitchen on Saturdays, and you could choose another task. What do you think? Let us review the plan in two weeks. Thanks again for being honest with me.

Hello Sam, thanks for telling me how you feel. Your message suggests that I am not doing enough, and I can see why you are upset. Admittedly, I have not cleaned much lately, and I am sorry about that. Still, my new job means that I work late most evenings, so perhaps the real problem is time, not effort. I am not sure that a strict rule would help, but a simple calendar might. What if we share the tasks by day, and I take the bathroom and the kitchen at weekends? We could try it for a month and then check whether it works for both of us. I would also like us to be more open with each other, because small problems grow when nobody talks about them. I hope that sounds fair, and thank you for being patient with me. Let us talk about it over dinner this week, and then we can write the calendar together.

feedback.es: Una buena respuesta interpreta lo implícito, agradece, concede un punto, defiende la postura con cautela y propone un plan concreto.

origin.text: Caso final. Tu compañero de casa escribe: «Some of us seem to do all the cleaning while others are always out.» Escribe entre 160 y 270 palabras: interpreta lo que implica, agradece, reconoce un punto, defiende tu postura con cautela (tu horario de trabajo te deja poco tiempo) y propón un plan (un calendario) con un acuerdo concreto.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Entiendo tu preocupación; sin embargo, mantengo mi postura.»

answer.text: I understand your concern nevertheless I keep my position

feedback.es: Se reconoce primero la preocupación y nevertheless marca el contraste: se mantiene la postura sin romper la cortesía.

prompt.es: Elige la respuesta con más tacto y matiz a la propuesta.

choices.text: Thank you for the idea. I admit it helps some people, but eight is hard for parents.
I take issue with this plan. Eight is far too early, and I am sure that everybody agrees with me.
Thanks, eight is fine. I will tell the others, even though I think that it is quite unfair.

feedback.es: Agradece, admite un punto a favor y expone el problema con matiz; las otras respuestas confrontan o ceden en contra de su opinión.

origin.text: Your manager proposes moving the weekly meeting to eight in the morning. Several colleagues have small children, and you think the plan is unfair, but you want to stay on good terms.

prompt.es: Escucha el mensaje y elige cómo suena la hablante.

choices.text: Enthusiastic: she is pleased to have one more meeting this week.
Sarcastic: she is unhappy about the plan and says the opposite.
Neutral: she is reporting the new time without any opinion about it.

feedback.es: «Oh, brilliant… Just what we needed» es sarcasmo: dice lo contrario de lo que siente, porque no quiere otra reunión a las ocho; no es entusiasmo ni un aviso neutral.

origin.audio: Oh, brilliant. Another meeting at eight in the morning. Just what we needed after the week we have had. I am sure everybody will be thrilled to give up their Friday evening too.
